newsitem.title: USA: SEARS JULY DOMESTIC SAME STORE SALES RISE.
newsitem.headline: SEARS JULY DOMESTIC SAME STORE SALES RISE.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Thursday that its same store sales for the four weeks ended August 2, 1997 rose 2.4 percent from the comparable period a year ago.
Total domestic sales in July increased 5.9 percent to $2.09 billion from $1.98 billion in sales generated in the four weeks ended August 3, 1996, the retailer said.

"Women's ready to wear and footwear continued to lead growth in our apparel business, while cosmetics and fragrances again achieved double-digit increases," said Arthur Martinez, chairman and chief executive officer, in a news release.

"Hardlines increases in full-line stores were led by appliances, while off-the-mall Dealer stores reported a double-digit comparable store sales increase, led by appliances and lawn and garden equipment," he said.

"Automotive stores experienced a decrease, primarily due to the ongoing conversion of free-standing tire stores to the NTB (National Tire and Battery) format as well as conversion of Western Auto retail stores to the Parts America format," Martinez said.
For the four weeks ending August 2, 1997 Sears reported total revenues of $2.94 billion, 8.6 percent above the $2.71 billion in the prior-year period.
For the 26 weeks ending August 2, Sears reported total revenues of $18.64 billion, 7.1 percent above the $17.41 billion in the prior-year period.
